I have been growing stevia on this land for many years now. My children help off-farm, so it is mostly just my wife and me managing the 6 mu. At my age and with my experience, I know exactly what this crop needs and I do not waste inputs.

Quzhou is dry — the well is essential. Stevia roots do not like waterlogging but they suffer badly if I let the soil dry out too long in summer. I irrigate carefully and consistently.

I switched to improved varieties years ago because the stevioside content is meaningfully higher and the buyers at the processing station pay by grade. Traditional seeds make no sense for me anymore. I do rotary tillage before transplanting seedlings in April — the soil needs to be loose and aerated for good root establishment. I apply base fertilizer at transplanting and then topdress after the first cutting in July.

Stevia does not need heavy nitrogen — too much and the plants go leggy and the leaf-to-stem ratio drops. I keep nitrogen moderate, push slightly more potassium because it helps with stevioside accumulation and stress tolerance. I plan two cuttings this season: first in late July, second in early October before the frost risk rises.

With well irrigation and careful scheduling, I irrigate about 7 times across the season. Pest pressure is manageable — mainly aphids and some fungal issues in humid stretches — so 3 pesticide applications is my normal practice.
